JOB SUMMARY

Spend your summer at the center of how Molina builds and supports its provider network. This 10-week, paid internship pairs you with Provider Relations professionals at work that reaches real providers and members — provider outreach and education, network performance analytics, and process improvement. You will own a project from question to recommendation, present your findings to leaders, and leave with healthcare industry insight, a professional network, and experience you can point to on day one of your career.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Partner with Provider Relations on outreach, education and onboarding support for our provider network.
  • Research and help resolve provider inquiries, and help prepare provider communications and training materials.
  • Sit in on joint operating committee and provider meetings, capture follow-ups, and see how partnerships are managed.
  • Support network adequacy, access and performance reporting, including provider data validation and Excel/Power BI dashboards.
  • Turn analysis into clear, concise recommendations for non-technical audiences.
  • Projects may include: a provider directory accuracy audit, a network adequacy dashboard refresh, a provider onboarding/education toolkit, or a JOC reporting package refresh.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • Curious, self-motivated and comfortable asking questions in a fast-moving team.
  • Clear, professional written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and good time management across multiple priorities.
  • Comfort with MS Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and internet research; interest in data and analytics a plus.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem solving, and the judgment to handle confidential information in compliance with HIPAA.

REQUIRED EDUCATION

  • Candidate must be currently enrolled in an undergraduate program, should be a freshman or sophomore with a minimum GPA of 3.0 or higher.
  • Able to commit to the full-time, 10-week internship program
  • Candidate must possess unrestricted authorization to work in the United States.

Blake Willson Group (BWG) unites deep domain experts with technologists who leverage industry-leading financial management solutions to address the most critical mission objectives. Headquartered in the National Capital Region, the firm delivers measurable outcomes through technology-forward strategies and advanced solutions that drive mission success.

Blake Willson Group has a distinguished track record of exceptional performance, achieving operational efficiencies that allow our clients to do more with less. BWG has earned the confidence of its clients by consistently exceeding expectations through its unwavering commitment to best value solutions, implemented with speed.

Job Location:

This role is 100% remote.

Clearance:

Must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and have the ability to obtain a Public Trust Security Clearance.

Job Description:

Blake Willson Group is seeking a Senior Healthcare Actuarial Consultant to support the evaluation of complex healthcare proposals for a major federal procurement. The consultant will apply hands-on experience with healthcare data, cost and utilization models, reimbursement, pricing, risk adjustment, and rate development to independently evaluate proposals and supporting analyses. Working with a Senior Pricing Consultant, the consultant will translate complex healthcare data and analytical findings into clear recommendations supporting proposal evaluation, clarifications, negotiations, and source selection. The ideal candidate will have recent hands-on healthcare modeling and data analysis experience and the ability to independently assess assumptions, methodologies, and supporting data. In this position, you will also:

  • Evaluate healthcare proposal pricing, cost models, rate-development methodologies, utilization, reimbursement, trend, risk adjustment, and supporting data.
  • Review solicitation requirements, evaluation criteria, data specifications, amendments, Government assumptions, and other acquisition documentation.
  • Analyze claims, encounter, eligibility, membership, provider, utilization, reimbursement, and other healthcare data for quality, completeness, consistency, and reasonableness.
  • Review, modify, maintain, test, and independently validate healthcare analytical and pricing models, including formulas, assumptions, inputs, outputs, and model logic.
  • Evaluate healthcare cost projections and identify key drivers, anomalies, unsupported assumptions, methodological limitations, data deficiencies, and financial risks.
  • Perform calculations, reconciliations, sensitivity analyses, scenario testing, benchmarking, and other analytical procedures to assess proposed results.
  • Compare proposal assumptions and results against historical experience, Government assumptions, independent estimates, market data, and other relevant benchmarks.
  • Develop clarification questions, written findings, and recommendations addressing data, modeling, methodology, pricing, and potential financial risks.
  • Collaborate with the Senior Pricing Consultant and acquisition team to support proposal evaluations, negotiations, source selection, and analysis of proposal revisions and FPRs.
  • Maintain traceable workpapers and communicate clear analytical findings to technical, financial, acquisition, and Government stakeholders while protecting sensitive information.

Required Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Healthcare Analytics, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of experience in healthcare actuarial analysis, managed-care analytics, healthcare economics, reimbursement, claims analytics, healthcare pricing, data analytics, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of recent hands-on experience developing, maintaining, materially modifying, testing, or independently validating healthcare cost, utilization, reimbursement, pricing, or rate-development models, including direct analysis of underlying healthcare data and assumptions.

Desired Skills:

  • Experience evaluating another organization's healthcare pricing, rates, actuarial submissions, reimbursement proposals, analytical models, or underlying assumptions for a purchaser, regulator, health plan, Government agency, or advisory client.
  • Experience supporting federal or state healthcare procurements, proposal evaluations, price analysis, clarification development, negotiation support, source selection, or related acquisition activities.
  • Experience with Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, VA Community Care, FEHB, commercial managed care, or other large-scale healthcare programs, including medical, dental, pharmacy, health-plan, TPA, or provider-network environments.
  • Experience analyzing healthcare data, including claims, encounter, eligibility, membership, provider, reimbursement, and utilization data, and performing data validation, reconciliation, trend analysis, benchmarking, sensitivity analysis, or scenario modeling.
  • Experience using SQL, SAS, R, Python, Power BI, Power Query, Excel, or other analytical, actuarial, modeling, or business intelligence tools, with the ability to develop clear analytical reports, proposal findings, price analyses, or negotiation-support materials.
  • ASA or FSA designation, membership in the American Academy of Actuaries, active progress toward an actuarial credential, or substantial equivalent healthcare actuarial experience, with demonstrated ability to communicate complex analytical findings and deliver accurate, traceable products under compressed procurement timelines.

We Do Consulting Differently


The Policy Analyst position is a staff consulting position within Berkeley Research Group’s Healthcare Transactions and Strategy (HTS) practice.

HTS provides healthcare policy, regulatory, reimbursement, and data analytics advisory services to healthcare organizations, investors, and other stakeholders. This position will primarily support Washington, DC–based policy teams, using research and quantitative analysis to inform policy development, evaluate policy proposals, and assess their implications for healthcare stakeholders.

We are seeking a highly motivated problem solver who combines an understanding of healthcare policy with strong quantitative and research skills. The successful candidate will translate complex policy and business questions into practical research and analysis plans, interpret findings, and develop clear recommendations for clients.


The role involves both qualitative and quantitative work, with a particular focus on Medicare, Medicaid, and healthcare reimbursement. Assignments may include developing and evaluating policy options, modeling the effects of proposed legislative and regulatory changes, and analyzing healthcare claims and public data to inform policy recommendations. The analyst will work closely with policy experts and data analytics colleagues to translate complex findings into clear, evidence-based guidance for clients.


Job Responsibilities

  • Research and interpret federal and state healthcare legislation, regulations, payment policies, and program guidance, and assess their implications for clients.
  • Support policy development by identifying and evaluating policy options, testing key assumptions, and developing evidence-based recommendations.
  • Define the evidence needed to evaluate a policy proposal, select appropriate datasets and methods, and assess effects on spending, utilization, access, and affected stakeholders.
  • Develop specifications for the data analytics team that explain the policy question, study population, measures, comparison groups, and assumptions; work with analysts to resolve methodological questions and interpret results.
  • Conduct analyses that quantify the impact of policy and reimbursement changes on healthcare organizations, patient populations, and government spending.
  • Develop Excel-based models to evaluate payment methodologies, estimate financial impacts, and compare policy scenarios.
  • Validate results against source materials, published benchmarks, and expected payment or utilization patterns; investigate discrepancies and document limitations.
  • Assess what the evidence supports, identify trade-offs among policy options, and explain how findings should inform a client’s policy position or next steps.
  • Prepare client-ready PowerPoint presentations, written summaries, tables, and data visualizations, and present findings to internal teams and clients.
  • Take ownership of assigned work streams, establish priorities with project leaders, and flag methodological or delivery issues before they affect the engagement.
  • Contribute to proposals, scopes of work, policy research, and the development of new analytical approaches and tools.

Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree in public policy, public health, economics, healthcare management, statistics, mathematics, business, or a related field is required. A relevant graduate degree is preferred.
  • A minimum of four years of relevant experience in healthcare consulting, policy research, government, a healthcare organization, or a comparable analytical setting.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting quantitative research or data analysis to address healthcare policy, reimbursement, or business questions.
  • Working knowledge of Medicare and/or Medicaid, including how coverage, payment, and program requirements affect healthcare providers, payers, and beneficiaries.
  • Knowledge of Medicare and Medicaid research claims data, including their structure, appropriate uses, and limitations for healthcare policy, reimbursement, and utilization analyses.
  • Experience interpreting healthcare regulations, payment methodologies, or other technical policy materials and explaining their practical implications.
  • Experience supporting healthcare policy development or evaluating legislative and regulatory proposals is preferred.

Required Skills

  • Strong quantitative, analytical, research, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify and question assumptions.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including building and reviewing analytical models, and proficiency in PowerPoint and Word.
  • Ability to develop clear analysis specifications and work effectively with technical colleagues. Experience using SAS, SQL, R, Stata, or comparable analytical tools is preferred.
  • Ability to synthesize policy research and analytical results into concise, practical findings for audiences with different levels of technical knowledge.
  • Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Commitment to accurate, well-supported work, with careful attention to detail and documentation.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently with appropriate guidance, and exercise judgment about when to seek input from project leaders.
  • Intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and a desire to work collaboratively across policy and analytics teams.
